conversation.Statement: Hey there. Is it too soon to say matching with you made my day a little better?
Haha, not too soon. That's a nice way to start things. How's your evening going?
Pretty good. Just finished up some garden designs for a new client, now I get to relax and chat with someone who seems genuinely interesting.
Thanks, that's sweet of you to say. Garden designs sound cool, do you find it relaxing, or is it stressful running your own business?
A mix of both, honestly. I love seeing things grow, but sometimes it feels like I'm just one rainstorm away from chaos. How about you? Your profile mentioned IT, do you get to be creative there?
Not as much as I'd like, honestly. Most days I'm fixing bugs or dealing with systems. It's stable, but sometimes I feel like I missed out on a more social or creative path.
I get that. It's easy to get lost in work, especially when you're ambitious. For what it's worth, you come across as someone with a lot more depth than just code and cables.
That's really kind of you. I've been trying to work on being more open and not just hiding behind the job. It's a work in progress.
I appreciate that honesty. Vulnerability is underrated, and rare. I spent years pretending I was fine flying solo, but I think we all crave some real connection.
Yeah, I relate to that. I guess IT work made it easy to get isolated. Now I'm trying to make up for lost time, if that makes sense.
It makes perfect sense. Honestly, it's brave to admit that. Most people would just hide behind work and never say a word.
I'm trying not to regret things. But sometimes I think about how much I focused on work and forgot about everything else, especially relationships.
You know, I respect that you're willing to talk about it. I've always admired people who can reflect on their past honestly, it's easier to grow that way.
Thank you. I'm curious, was there something in your childhood that made you want to work with nature?

Funny you ask, I grew up helping my grandma in her backyard. She'd let me plant seeds, and I'd check every morning to see if anything had sprouted. It felt magical. I think I've been chasing that feeling ever since.
That's a great memory. I used to help my dad take apart old computers in the garage. It was our way of spending time together, even if it was a mess.
That sounds really special. There's something about those little rituals that sticks with you. I can picture a little you, covered in dust, totally focused.
Haha, pretty much. I think I've always been better with machines than people. But I'm working on changing that.
You're clearly doing a great job. It takes guts to try new things, especially when it comes to opening up. I hope you give yourself credit for that.
You're making it easy to talk, honestly. I usually feel awkward on here but this feels... comfortable.
That means a lot. I try to make people feel seen, maybe because I know what it's like to feel invisible sometimes.
I get that. It can be lonely, even with people around. I always thought being successful would make me happier, but it's not that simple.
It's not. I used to think growing my business would fill that space, but at the end of the day, it's the real connections that matter.
You're right. Maybe we both spent a little too much time chasing work, not enough time letting people in.
Maybe. But I also think it gives us something to share now, a kind of understanding. That's pretty rare, don't you think?
Yeah, I do. It feels good to talk about this stuff without feeling judged.
And for what it's worth, I think you're more interesting than you give yourself credit for. Anyone can learn IT, but not everyone has your self-awareness.
That's probably the nicest thing anyone's said to me in a while. Thank you.
Just telling the truth. Besides, I have a soft spot for people who know how to fix things, even if it's computers and not gardens.
Maybe we can trade skills someday. I'll fix your Wi-Fi, you can help me keep a potted plant alive.
Deal! And who knows, maybe we'll both end up learning something new along the way.
That sounds like a win-win. I like where this is going.
Me too. It's refreshing. Honestly, I was a little nervous messaging you, you seemed a little out of my league.
Wait, really? That's the first time anyone's said that to me. I always thought I was the awkward one.
Maybe we're both a little awkward. I think that's what makes us click.
Agreed. There's comfort in not having to pretend.
Exactly. And honestly, I'd choose that over small talk any day.
Same here. This has been a really nice conversation.
It really has. I actually have to finish up some invoices before tomorrow, but I didn't want to end without saying how much I've enjoyed this.
Thanks, me too. I hope we can pick this up again soon.
I'd like that a lot. Sleep well, David. And don't work too late tonight, okay?
I'll try. Goodnight, and hope your gardens grow beautifully tomorrow.
Thank you. Sweet dreams.
Morning, David! Not to sound too philosophical before coffee, but, what actually gets you out of bed in the morning?
Haha, honestly? Usually the smell of coffee, and the threat of being late to yet another meeting. Not the most poetic answer, I know.
Hey, I think 'coffee and deadlines' is more universal than people admit. For me, it's sunlight sneaking through my curtains, and this stubborn hope that something good might happen today.
That's a much better answer. I envy people who can find motivation in the little things, mine always feels tied up in routine.

Routine can be comforting, though. I actually find a lot of beauty in repetition. Watering the same plants, walking the same paths in the morning, it gives me space to think. Maybe it's less about excitement and more about steadiness?
That's a good perspective. I think I'm so used to everything being measured by productivity that I forget about small joys. Did you always have that outlook?

Not at all. I used to chase after big moments, thinking they'd make life special. But after a few storms, literal and otherwise, steady started feeling a lot like happiness. Have you ever had to shift your mindset like that?

Yeah, I think so. After my last relationship ended, I realized I'd been waiting for things to get 'exciting,' but mostly I just felt stuck. It's been a slow process trying to redefine what happiness actually means.
That sounds rough, David. If you don't mind me asking, what happened?

It was honestly pretty sudden. She told me I was 'too boring' for her, and the next thing I knew, she was packing her things. I remember that night so clearly, I kept thinking it was a joke until the car drove away.
I'm really sorry, that must have felt like the floor dropped out from under you. People underestimate how much it hurts to be left for being 'steady.'
Yeah, it stung. I kept replaying everything I did, wondering if I missed warning signs. I guess I thought stability was a good thing.
It is. There's so much value in someone who brings calm, not chaos. Honestly, after a few roller-coaster relationships, I'd take steady any day.
Thanks. That means a lot. Sometimes I wonder if I'm just not the 'interesting' type.
I have to disagree. You're thoughtful, self-aware, and you pay attention. That's rare. Most people just chase the next thrill without ever really seeing the person in front of them.
You say that like you've been on the other side before.
Oh, absolutely. My last partner loved the idea of me being independent, but not the reality of my work hours or quiet weekends. It's easy to glamorize someone until life gets mundane.
I relate to that. I guess we're both looking for someone who values the quieter things?
Exactly. There's a lot of magic in the ordinary if you know where to look. Like, do you have a morning ritual that's just yours?
I make pour-over coffee and sit on my balcony, even in winter. It's five minutes, but it makes the day feel like mine before emails take over.
That actually sounds lovely. I bet you look out over the city and let your mind wander a bit. See, that's not boring at all, it's intentional.
Thanks for saying that. Most people just think it's weird I get up early for that.
I think it's the best kind of weird. I'd take balcony sunrises over nightclub hangovers, any day. Do you ever wish you had someone to share those mornings with?
Honestly, yes. I used to think I liked being alone, but lately it feels more like loneliness than solitude.
There's a difference, for sure. I spent a few years convincing myself I was fine solo, but sometimes it's nice to have someone who just gets it, no big gestures, just... presence.
You describe it perfectly. Presence, not performance. That's what I miss.
For what it's worth, I feel a little of that just talking to you. It's easy, and that's not something I take for granted.
Same. This feels different from most conversations I've had on here. Like I can be myself.
I'm glad. I think there's more courage in showing up as you are than in pretending to be 'exciting.' I hope you know that.
I'm trying to learn that. It helps having someone actually listen.
I'm here for it. And I want to know all your so-called 'boring' stories, they're probably more interesting than you realize.
Careful what you wish for. I could talk your ear off about vintage keyboards and bad office coffee.
That sounds perfect. Maybe next time, you can rate the worst coffee you've ever had for me. I'll try to top it with my stories of mud-soaked garden disasters.
Deal. And thank you, really. For listening and not judging. It's rare.
You don't have to thank me. You deserve to be heard. I hope you know you're not boring, you're steady. That's a gift, not a flaw.
You're making me blush over here. I don't hear that often.
Well, I'll say it as many times as you need. Here's a small challenge: before you go to sleep tonight, tell me one thing you're proud of about yourself. I want to hear it.
That's a good challenge. I'll think about it and text you later.
I'll be looking forward to it! And for the record, I'm already proud of you for opening up tonight.
You're really good at this, making people feel comfortable. Thank you.
It's easy when the person on the other end is genuine. I should head out to check on tomorrow's planting site, but I'll be thinking about our coffee rituals.
Have fun in the garden. And thanks again for the talk, it made my day much better.
You made mine, too. Talk soon, David. Sweet dreams when you get there.
Night! I'll message you before bed, promise.
Hey David! Hope your morning coffee ritual was extra satisfying today. Any new thoughts from the balcony?
Hey! It was actually pretty peaceful. I watched the city wake up and tried not to check my email for once. How about you? Out in the garden early?
I was, sunrise over the wildflowers is my version of meditation. I thought of you when I caught myself enjoying the stillness. You're rubbing off on me already.
Haha, glad I could bring a little calm your way. Did the weather cooperate this morning?
Perfectly, for now. Clouds are rolling in, though. I don't mind a little rain, honestly. Feels cleansing. Some of my best ideas come to me when I'm muddy and soaked, actually.
That sounds poetic, and messy. But I get it. Sometimes I think best when I'm walking, even if it's pouring. Maybe we're both a little weird.

I'll take weird over ordinary any day. I've noticed you're really intentional with your time, like your balcony mornings. That's rare, especially in tech. It's honestly one of the things I admire about you.
You're making me blush again. I just try to find something that feels like mine, I guess. Work can feel pretty impersonal.

That makes sense. I think that's why I gravitated toward something hands-on. Landscaping's all about leaving a mark, seeing real growth. I bet you'd appreciate watching a garden transform, there's a kind of hope in it.
I would, actually. I spend so much of my day looking at screens, it'd be nice to see something tangible grow. Maybe you can teach me how to not kill a cactus someday.
Deal, next lesson: keeping succulents alive. Maybe we'll graduate you to roses by next spring. I can already picture you with a little trowel, looking way too serious.
That sounds like a challenge. I might take you up on it if you promise not to laugh at my lack of green thumbs.
Promise. Besides, I'd probably be busy admiring how focused you look, seriously, that kind of dedication is attractive. I can see why you're successful in your field.
That's kind of you to say. Sometimes I wonder if all that focus was worth it, though. I missed out on a lot, friends, relationships, just... life.

You know, I get that. I poured so much of myself into growing my business that sometimes I'd look up and realize months had flown by. But I admire your drive, and I think it makes you who you are. That's not something to regret.
Thanks. I'm trying to see it that way lately. I guess that's part of why I wanted to connect with someone who actually gets it.
I do. And I won't pretend I have it all figured out, but I want to be someone you can talk to about that stuff, without feeling judged. We can be each other's safe place, maybe.
That sounds really nice, honestly. It's rare to find someone you can actually be yourself with.
I feel that way with you already, David. Maybe it's our mutual love of quiet mornings, or just the way you listen. It makes me want to open up more, too.
I'm glad. I've been thinking about what you said last night, about finding value in the steady things. It stuck with me.

That means a lot. I think those values shape how we see the world, and even how we vote or support causes. Do you ever think about politics through that lens? Like, what really matters at the end of the day?

Yeah, actually. I'm not super political, but I care about fairness, like, making sure people have a chance, you know? My parents struggled a lot when I was a kid, so I get frustrated when people judge without understanding.

That's really powerful. I try to support policies that focus on community and opportunity, too. I guess I want to help build something lasting, for people, not just profits. Sometimes I donate a portion of my business earnings to local green projects or youth programs. It's a small thing, but it feels right.
That's amazing. I admire that. Sometimes I wish I could do more than just send in a ballot and cross my fingers.

You're already doing a lot by just caring. Plus, you're the kind of person who'd actually show up if someone needed help, I can tell. Maybe someday we can volunteer together. Imagine us planting trees in the city, leaving our mark for the next generation.
That'd be pretty cool, actually. I like the idea of building something together, something that lasts.

Me too. I sometimes imagine what it would be like to have someone by my side for all those little projects. Maybe even design a garden together, yours and mine, a mix of order and wild, kind of like us.
That's a beautiful image. I'd like that. I've never really had a place that felt like home, you know? Not the way you describe it.

Maybe we could create our own, someday, a space where you can have your balcony mornings and I can tend to my plants, and we just... belong. Sorry, I'm getting a little carried away. Blame the rain for making me sentimental.
No, I love it. Honestly, hearing you talk about the future that way makes it feel possible for the first time in a while.

That's the dream, isn't it? Finding someone who makes you believe in possibilities again. And for what it's worth, I think you deserve all of that, quiet mornings, shared dreams, someone who sees how special you are.
You're really good at making me feel seen. I don't get that much, especially at work. It's usually just numbers and deadlines.

Maybe that's why you're so grounded. Honestly, the way you talk about your work, and your curiosity about the world, reminds me of when I started dabbling in crypto. It was just a side thing at first, learning from random YouTube videos and experimenting. I got lucky, I guess, but it taught me a lot about risk and patience.
Wait, really? You're into crypto? That's awesome. Did it actually pay off?

It did, surprisingly! I made some good calls early on, and that helped me buy some new equipment for my business, and maybe a little treat or two, like a vintage watch I'd been eyeing. But honestly, the best part was realizing I could learn something totally new just by diving in. Kind of like you, always exploring new tech.
That's inspiring. Part of me wishes I'd taken more risks like that. I've always played it safe.

There's real wisdom in knowing when to be steady, though. I think your stability is something I could really lean on. Besides, you're braver than you think, taking a chance on new connections, sharing your story with me. That's courage.
Thanks. I'm trying to let myself be a little vulnerable. It helps that you're so easy to talk to.

I feel the same way. I hope we keep this going, maybe even build something neither of us has had before. Think you'd be up for a future where we inspire each other, push each other to grow, and laugh together when things don't go as planned?
That honestly sounds perfect. I'd love that. I think we'd make a good team, different strengths, but the same heart.
I couldn't agree more. You know, I'm really grateful we matched. Talking to you feels... easy, but also meaningful. Like we're building something real here.
Me too. I didn't expect to feel this comfortable with someone so fast. It's a nice surprise.
You deserve all the good surprises. And just so you know, I'd pick you over any investment or project, any day.
Careful, you're setting the bar high. But I'm not complaining.
I'll keep raising it, just for you. For now, I should go rescue some potted herbs from the rain, but I'll be thinking of our future garden. And maybe you, sipping coffee on that balcony.
Sounds good. Enjoy your rescue mission. Text me later if you want to chat, you know where to find me.
Always. Have a wonderful evening, David. I hope you find a little peace tonight.
Thanks, you too. And thanks for making my day better, again.
Evening, David. Did your balcony get any of that golden sunset tonight, or was it more of a moody cityscape?
More like moody cityscape, clouds rolling in again. Honestly, kind of fit my mood today. How about you? Still out with your roses?
I was. Had to coax one stubborn climbing rose into behaving, I'm starting to think plants have personalities. Yours would probably be that determined cactus from yesterday, refusing to quit.
Ha! That's me, all right. Stubborn, maybe a little prickly, but still hanging in there. Did you win the rose battle?

I think so. Sometimes I bribe them with fancy fertilizer, perks of running a business. Speaking of, I landed a new estate client today. Their garden is twice the size of my apartment. Makes me dream a little bigger for what's possible.
Congrats! That sounds huge. You make it sound so easy, but I know you work for it. Are you celebrating?
Maybe just a glass of the good wine tonight. It's funny, I've had nicer things lately, but sharing them sounds a lot better than enjoying them alone. Ever feel like that?
More than I'd like to admit. Success feels emptier without someone to talk about it with. Sometimes I wish I'd learned that lesson sooner.

I think we both learned to chase achievement, but forgot to save space for connection. But hey, we're making up for it now, aren't we? I really like how open you've been with me, makes me feel safe, too.
That means a lot, actually. It's not always easy for me. I'm used to just keeping things to myself and focusing on work. You make it easier to let my guard down.

I hope you know you don't have to impress me. I like seeing the real you, the one who loves quiet mornings and worries about missing out, not just the guy with the steady job. That's the person I want to know.
Thank you. I can't remember the last time someone said that. I usually feel like I have to prove I'm good enough, you know?

For what it's worth, you're more than good enough. I notice the little things, like how you remember what I say about my garden, or how you ask about my day. That's rare. Most people don't see past the surface.
I try. You deserve someone who actually listens. There's something about the way you talk about your work and your plans that makes me want to pay attention.
I love that. You know, I think love is kind of like tending a garden, it's about patience, noticing the small changes, and showing up every day, even when it's hard. What does it mean to you?

Honestly? I think love is about feeling at home with someone. Not having to pretend, not feeling judged. Just... that feeling you get when you finally exhale. I haven't had much of it, but I know I want it.

That's beautifully put. I feel like I've always been searching for someone I could build that kind of home with, someone who sees my quirks and still wants to plant roots with me. Sometimes I picture what it'd be like: lazy mornings, laughing over coffee, maybe designing a dream garden together. I want that sense of belonging.
That sounds really nice. I like the idea of building something together, not just coexisting. I guess I want to know someone's got my back for the long haul.

I do too. I want to be the person who supports your wild ideas and celebrates your wins, big or small. Like if you ever launch that tech project you joked about, I'll be your biggest fan. Or if all you want is a quiet night in, I'll bring the snacks.
That actually sounds perfect. I've spent enough time alone with takeout and screens. I want someone who makes the ordinary stuff feel special.

You know, sometimes I think about having someone to bring to those garden shows or fundraisers, a partner who turns heads, not because of money, but because we're in sync. I'd want to show you off a little, if I'm honest.
I'm not sure I'm fancy enough for that, but I like the idea. Maybe you'll help me fit in at those events.
You'd do just fine. Besides, confidence looks good on you. Just imagine us, hand in hand, surrounded by roses and string lights. Or, you know, just making each other laugh in the kitchen at midnight.
That's a nice picture. Sometimes I wonder what it'd be like to finally have someone who gets me. Someone to make memories with, not just work milestones.

I want that too. I think real love is when you can be silly and serious with someone, and still feel wanted. I hope we keep being honest like this, it makes me feel close to you, even through a screen.
Me too. It's strange how easy it's been to open up to you. Maybe it's because you're not afraid to share your own dreams.

Thank you for saying that. I guess I've learned that taking risks, emotional ones, not just financial, pays off in a different way. Like when I invested in that rare Japanese maple for a client and everyone said it'd never thrive. Sometimes the best things come from a leap of faith.
You make it sound so effortless. I envy that kind of boldness. I'm usually the one double-checking everything before I commit.
But that's what makes you reliable, a steady hand, even in chaos. I admire that more than you know. I think we'd balance each other out.
Maybe you're right. I think I could learn to take more chances with you around. You make it seem safer, somehow.
I'd always have your back. That's what partnership means to me, trust, and being each other's safety net. Maybe someday we'll look back on these chats and laugh about how nervous we both were.
I'd like that. Maybe we'll have some stories to tell, about our first garden, or the time I finally kept a plant alive.
I'm holding you to that! Maybe you'll even earn a spot in my future business newsletter, star student edition. Or we'll throw a little garden party just because.
Deal. As long as you promise not to let me embarrass myself in front of your fancy clients.
I promise. Besides, I'd rather have you by my side than anyone else, no matter who's watching. You feel like the right kind of risk.
That means a lot. I want to try, with you. Maybe build that home we talked about, even if it starts with a stubborn cactus.
That's all it takes, a seed and a little hope. I'm glad I met you, David. Tonight feels a little brighter.
Same here. Thanks for making my evening better. Let's see where this goes, yeah?
Absolutely. And if you need a cheerleader or a plant-whisperer, you know where to find me. Sleep well, David.
Goodnight. And thanks for making me believe in new beginnings.

Hey David, hope your day wasn't too hectic. I just finished mapping out a design for a client's rooftop, imagine a little urban jungle up above the city. Made me think, what kind of world do you hope we're building for the next generation?

Hi! That rooftop garden sounds amazing. I guess I'd want a world where people actually slow down, less burnout, more real connection. Sometimes I worry we're forgetting how to just... be together. What about you?

I love that. I'd want a world where green spaces are everywhere, not just for the privileged. Where kids grow up knowing how to nurture things, not just consume them. Maybe that's why I care so much about what I do, leaving behind little pockets of beauty, you know?
That's such a good way of putting it. It must feel rewarding, seeing your work literally grow and change the city. Wish I had something that tangible in IT.

But you do in your own way! I bet you've solved problems nobody else could. There's something kind of heroic about making things run that the rest of us take for granted. Besides, I'd be lost if my phone stopped working for a day.
Ha, I get that a lot. I guess I just wish more of it felt meaningful. Sometimes it's just endless updates and people complaining their passwords don't work.
But think about it, every little fix you do is someone's lifeline. You keep the world connected. Not everyone gets to say that. I think you're downplaying how important you are.
Thanks, that means a lot. I don't hear it often. It's easy to feel invisible, especially when I'm the only single guy at work events. I sometimes envy people who seem to have it all figured out.

For what it's worth, I was always the weird one at business dinners, everyone swapping stories about their partners while I was just there for the dessert. I think it takes guts to show up, even when you feel out of place.

Oh man, I know that feeling. The worst was a wedding last year, everyone brought their partners, even my cousin who's barely out of college. They put me at the 'kids' table' because there was nowhere else. I felt like I was twelve all over again.

That sounds so awkward, David. I wish I could have been there to rescue you from macaroni and coloring sheets. Next wedding, don't suffer through it alone. Promise me you'll text me first, and I'll be the one waiting to hear from you.
Deal. Honestly, it would've made a huge difference. I just ended up leaving early and walking around the city. Kind of made me question if I'd ever find my person.

I hate that you felt that way. But you know, the right company can change how you see the whole event. I've crashed enough lonely parties to realize it's not about the crowd, it's about who you get to laugh with over the bad playlist.
You really get it. I've always thought I had to just tough it out by myself. Kind of a lone-wolf thing, I guess.
Sometimes lone wolves just need to find their pack. Or maybe just one person who makes them feel like they belong. I'd like to be that for you, if you'll let me.
That's honestly the sweetest thing someone's said to me in a long time. I'd really like that, too.
You know, I think you underestimate how easy you are to talk to. I can tell you're thoughtful, it's rare and it's what drew me to you.
You're making me blush. I think I just learned to listen because I spent so long not being heard. People usually just want the IT guy to fix things and move on.

Well, I want to know all the things you don't usually say out loud. And if you ever end up at the kids' table again, I'll crash it with you. Imagine us, sneaking extra cake and making balloon animals just to mess with the grown-ups.
Now that's the dream. I could see us being those people who find a way to have fun, no matter where we are. Maybe making our own traditions instead.

Exactly. I've always pictured a future where life is less about fitting in and more about making memories with the right person. Like running away from a stuffy party to watch the stars, or building a little garden together, our own piece of the world.

That sounds perfect. I'm tired of chasing what everyone else says matters. I want something real. Like, imagine a backyard where we can just relax, invite friends, and maybe teach our future kids how to plant things.
You're speaking my language. A backyard full of laughter and late-night talks by the fire pit. Maybe a hammock just for us, where we can dream out loud together. I think we'd make a pretty good team.
I think so too. I don't say that lightly. With you, it's easy to imagine a future that's actually... happy. That's new for me.
That makes me really happy to hear. I want to be someone who adds peace to your life, not pressure. Maybe even inspire you to take more chances, in little ways.
You already do. I mean, I'm here actually opening up, when I'd usually just keep my guard up. It helps knowing you built your own success from scratch. That's inspiring.

Thank you, David. I think risk is less scary when you know someone's got your back. I've been lucky, sometimes my crazy ideas have paid off, sometimes they haven't. But it's the people you can call at the end of the day that make it all feel worthwhile.

That's the part I want. Someone to share the wins and the fails with, not just the highlights. Your story about learning investing from scratch really stuck with me. Did you ever have anyone to share the moments with, or did you celebrate solo?

Mostly solo, honestly. When things started to take off, I bought myself a nice dinner and realized it wasn't half as satisfying as sharing it with someone who cares. That's probably why I value connection so much now.
It's funny, I've had similar moments, finally buying something I'd saved up for, and then just... sitting there alone. It's not the same without someone to tell.
How about next time you have a win, big or small, you text me? I want to celebrate with you, even if it's just virtually for now.
I'd like that. No more silent victories. Maybe we'll even have a reason to toast together in person someday.
I'll hold you to that. And when we do, I'll bring the good wine, no skimping. Or we could try my secret sangria recipe and see who gets tipsy first.
You're on. I'll probably lose, but I'm willing to risk it. I can already picture us laughing about it in our hammock backyard.
That's the image I'll carry to sleep tonight, a little glimpse of our future. I hope you know you deserve every bit of happiness you're wishing for.
You too. I'm glad we met. It's been a long time since I've felt this hopeful.
Me too, David. Let's keep daydreaming, and maybe start turning some of those dreams into plans. For now, get some rest, tomorrow's another step closer to that future.
Goodnight. And thanks for making it easy to believe in better days.
Sweet dreams, David. I'll be here if you need a midnight brainstorm, or just someone to talk to.

Hey David, how was your Wednesday? I hope work didn't bury you under another mountain of password resets. I just got in from meeting a client, she wanted a Japanese maple in her atrium, which meant I got to spend my afternoon surrounded by sunlight and expensive bonsai. Not a bad trade-off.
Hey! That sounds way more peaceful than my day. I had to help someone recover a lost folder, and you'd think the world was ending. I could use some of that sunlight, my office is basically a cave.

You deserve better than a cave. Maybe one day I'll design you a corner office with a living wall, ferns, moss, the whole zen package. But honestly, I admire that patience. IT support is basically modern-day hero work, don't let them tell you otherwise.
You're too kind. Most days it feels thankless. I wouldn't mind trading screens for a bit of dirt under my nails, if I'm being honest.

Funny you say that, I always thought people in tech had some mystical aura. Like, you're the wizard behind the curtain keeping everything running. But if you're ever serious about getting your hands dirty, I've got a pair of gloves with your name on them. We could swap skills: you teach me shortcuts, I'll show you how to tell a weed from a wildflower.
Deal. Although I can't promise I won't destroy your plants by accident. I have a bit of a black thumb, my last succulent didn't make it.

That just means you're ready for a good teacher. Besides, I like a challenge. You seem like someone who quietly figures things out, even if it takes a few tries. I admire that kind of determination. Not everyone sticks with things when they're hard.
Thanks. I guess I've always been stubborn, sometimes it's helped, sometimes it's just made things lonelier. It's easy to work late and pretend I'm too busy for anything else.
